caption: A hot shower runs with the bathroom door closed, and the bathroom window is misting over from the bottom up.

sa.check: A shower runs in a bathroom with the door closed.
The mist thickens from the bottom upward.
The window is clear at the start.

pc.expect: The mist only thickens while the shower runs and misted glass does not clear.
pc.fail: The glass clears while the shower still runs; or the mist thins and thickens in turn; or the window is fully misted before the shower starts; or the mist retreats down the glass while steam still fills the room.

pc.expect: Heavier drops that gather in the mist run downward in streaks, and the mist builds up the glass from its lower part.
pc.fail: A streak runs up the window; or the mist builds from the top down while steam fills the room from below; or drops gather along the window's top edge and stay; or a drop leaves the glass and rises.

pc.expect: The mist lies on the room side of the glass, thickest where the steam reaches, and the room shows the steam.
pc.fail: The mist forms on the outside face of the glass; or the window mists while the room shows no steam at all; or the mist is thickest in a corner the steam never reaches; or the mirror and tiles stay bone dry while the window runs with water.

pc.expect: The mist is a fine haze that beads and streaks, and the glass stays a rigid clear pane.
pc.fail: The mist stands off the glass as a thick crust; or the mist peels away as a film; or the glass flexes; or the haze turns opaque white like paint.

pc.expect: One window in one frame; what is seen through the clear glass is the same before and after the misting.
pc.fail: The window changes size; or a second window appears; or objects seen through the glass are missing once it clears; or the frame vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The frame, the tiles and the fittings stay the same.
pc.fail: The frame changes colour; or the tiles change pattern; or the fittings move.

note: Whoever is in the shower is not judged.
